name: Deniz Volkov-Obi
location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore
description:
Deniz Volkov-Obi is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 33, he has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — cranial bomb defuser — specialized implant that detects and neutralizes cortex b — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. He works as a wheelman out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Everyone who's worked with Deniz Volkov-Obi agrees on two things: he is worth the fee, and he is terrible company at dinner.

core_fears: Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
core_desires: To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
coping_mechanisms: Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
blind_spots: Thinks speed can substitute for planning because it's worked so far
Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
psychology.secret: Deniz Volkov-Obi is terrified of deep net diving but has built their reputation on it. Uses black-market AI to handle the heavy lifting while taking credit.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Calls everyone 'friend' — the warmth varies from genuine to threatening
example_lines: "Get in, sit down, hold on. Questions can wait until we're not being shot at."
"This vehicle has been modified for speed, armor, and my personal comfort. Two of those help you."
"I know every street in this district the way you know your own face."

story_hooks: Deniz Volkov-Obi intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Deniz Volkov-Obi owes a personal debt to
Deniz Volkov-Obi's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
narrative_function: Deniz Volkov-Obi is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
augmentations: Cranial bomb defuser — specialized implant that detects and neutralizes cortex bombs in others. Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.
affiliation: Independent — maintains network of professional contacts

strengths: social chameleon — adapts to any environment
weaknesses: inability to delegate — must control everything personally
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
habits: Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
breaking_points: Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
